clue.text: Gently cooking fish — many fish

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
D is the Roman numeral for 500, so a large number
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A recipe note about poaching fish, warning that a great many fish are involved.
explanation.walkthrough: D standing for 'many' is the crossword habit of using a big Roman numeral (D = 500) for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle an egg or fish is to cook it slowly in water just below boiling.

clue.text: Pat worries about security to start with

parts.note: cares are worries

indicators.note: to start with picks the opening letter of the word security

explanation.surface: Someone frets about security from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a name, but it is the verb: a gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke gently, like a light pat.

clue.text: Leave a place of desolation

explanation.surface: Abandoning a bleak and empty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon, and a desert is a barren, empty region of sand or rock.

clue.text: Embassy gets reservists back into fighting unit

indicators.note: into says the turned-round letters go inside the fighting unit

parts.note: a legion is a large army unit

indicators.note: back means the reservists' letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An embassy hears that reservists are returning to a combat unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the reservists, and 'into' places them inside the fighting unit. The Territorial Army is the UK's volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A legation is a diplomatic mission headed by a minister, a lesser kind of embassy.

clue.text: Some fine educators live in poverty

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some good teachers are poorly paid and struggle to get by.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in want of the necessities of life is to be poor, so to live in poverty.

clue.text: Even-tempered cub leader held in check

indicators.note: held in says one piece is placed inside another, the check enclosing the cub's opening

parts.note: plaid is a chequered tartan pattern, so a check

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so the opening of cub is taken

explanation.surface: A Cub Scout leader who keeps the youngsters in check stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cub leader' reads like Akela of the Cub Scouts, but it only gives C, which 'held in' puts inside PLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A placid person is calm and not easily upset, which is what even-tempered means.

clue.text: One praising old Scots music-hall star

explanation.surface: An admirer of a Scottish variety entertainer of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who extols is one praising, and Sir Harry Lauder was a famous Scottish music-hall singer of the early 1900s.

clue.text: Woolly kind of corgi

explanation.surface: A fluffy breed of Welsh dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly is a knitted jumper, such as a buttoned one, and the Cardigan Welsh corgi is one of the two corgi breeds.

clue.text: Diplomatic initiative from market in France

parts.note: de is French for from, the 'in France' applying to both words
marché is the French word for market

explanation.surface: A diplomatic move that started in a French market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' asks for French words: DE for 'from' and MARCHE for 'market'.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a formal diplomatic step or representation made to a foreign government.

clue.text: Quit being submissive

explanation.surface: Someone has given up their job because they were too meek.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned is both the past tense of stepping down from a post and an adjective for accepting one's fate meekly.

clue.text: Enough voters question men with little hesitation

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, so men
um is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A meeting checks numbers by questioning the men present, with a little hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for 'men' is the crossword convention of other ranks, the ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the minimum number of members needed for a meeting's vote to be valid.

clue.text: Disconnect appliance and exit

explanation.surface: Switch off the machine and leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch off a device stops it working, and a road junction leading away from a main road is a way out.

clue.text: Odds on luxury hotel stocking a spray

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London

explanation.surface: Betting on whether a grand hotel keeps a scent spray in its rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Starting price is the bookmaker's odds as a race begins; the Ritz is a grand London hotel. 'stocking' only links the pieces to what they make.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritz is a quick squirt of liquid from an atomiser, a light spray.

clue.text: Better see a Canadian lake

explanation.surface: A tourist is told that a lake in Canada is the finest to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior means higher in quality, and Lake Superior is the largest of North America's Great Lakes, shared by Canada and the USA.

clue.text: A number of leavers come to grief

indicators.note: to come to grief is to be wrecked, so the letters of leavers are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Quite a few people quitting end up in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, an indefinite number.

clue.text: Firm initially distributing a German sedative

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word distributing

parts.note: eine is the German word for a

explanation.surface: A company starts distributing a German-made sleeping drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a German' means the German word for 'a', EINE, not a German person.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opium-derived drug that relieves pain and calms, used as a mild sedative.

clue.text: Food served in us field hospital?

explanation.surface: A dish served up in an American army hospital in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is mashed potato, a staple food, and M*A*S*H was a US Mobile Army Surgical Hospital, famous from the TV series.

clue.text: Lively nightclubs in sunny climes?

explanation.surface: Buzzing clubs in warm holiday destinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular lively venues are called the places to be, and the phrase read literally describes places where it is warm.

clue.text: Gee! Taking a classical language can be sticky

indicators.note: taking means holding something inside, so the language goes within the exclamation

parts.note: taken as written
Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that studying an ancient language can be tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky' looks like difficult, as in a sticky wicket, but means gluey.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatine dissolved in water sets into a jelly and can be tacky to the touch, used in glues.

clue.text: Such a device shouldn't let Peter down

definitions.text: Such a device shouldn't let Peter down

parts.words: Such a device shouldn't let Peter down
parts.note: peter is old slang for a safe; a device that should not fail the safe is one designed never to fail

explanation.surface: A gadget that won't disappoint a man called Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name, but it is criminal slang for a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanism designed to revert to a harmless state if something goes wrong is built so it cannot cause danger on failing.

clue.text: It may augur badly for old males

parts.note: men are males

explanation.surface: A gloomy prophecy that things look bad for the elderly men.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, often a sign of misfortune.

clue.text: Socialist banner signifying danger

explanation.surface: A left-wing flag waved as a warning of peril.
explanation.definitionFit: The red flag is the emblem and anthem of socialism, and a red warning flag tells people there is danger ahead.

clue.text: Stop talking to secure oneself in the car

definitions.text: to secure oneself in the car

explanation.surface: A driver tells a chatty passenger to be quiet and buckle up.
explanation.definitionFit: Belt up is British slang for shut up, and literally means fastening a seat strap.

clue.text: Cycle endlessly in a scanty costume

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off the word for cycle

parts.note: a bike is a bicycle, to cycle
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, so a single, a

explanation.surface: Someone cycling non-stop in skimpy swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from BIKE; 'a' gives I, the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit that covers very little.

clue.text: Come and listen

explanation.surface: An invitation to be present and pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be present at an event, and also to pay heed to what is said.

clue.text: Crab and peas spattered on the keyboard

indicators.note: spattered means splashed about, so the letters of crab and peas are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eating seafood at their desk has splashed crab and peas over the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spattered' shuffles CRAB and PEAS into the long key on a keyboard; 'and' simply joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bar at the bottom of a keyboard inserts a gap between words.

clue.text: Obvious time to take charge

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious

explanation.surface: It is clearly the moment for someone to take control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' is the legal sense: a plaint is the statement of a complaint brought before a court.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaint is a formal accusation or complaint in law, an old word for a lament as well.

clue.text: Bouncer for the dance

explanation.surface: A doorman working at a formal party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a toy that bounces, and a ball is also a formal dancing party.

clue.text: I tucked into duck spread — it's addictive

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so the letter O

indicators.note: tucked into says one piece goes inside the other, the I slipping inside duck plus spread

parts.note: pâté is a meat or fish paste spread on bread

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into duck pâté and can't stop eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating, but it puts I inside O + PATE. A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, notorious for causing dependence.

clue.text: Anti-Ezra movement by Jewish ascetic

indicators.note: movement means the letters of Anti-Ezra are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest movement against the biblical scribe Ezra joined by a devout Jew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' reads as a political campaign but signals rearranging ANTIEZRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nazarite was an Israelite under a vow to abstain from wine and haircuts, a biblical ascetic.

clue.text: Flat area in which to walk and exercise

parts.note: to step is to walk
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Describing open flat land suitable for walking and keeping fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassy plain, as in Central Asia.

clue.text: Songster depressed by prison sentence

indicators.note: by means next to, so the prison sentence stands beside the word for depressed

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed
bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time, is a spell in jail

explanation.surface: A singer is down in the dumps after being jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' for a prison term is British slang (bird-lime, rhyming slang for time).
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebird is a North American songbird, so a songster.
